title: Power Apps: modernised Personal settings experience in model-driven apps
summary: The briefing passes: its default state, licensing requirement and navigation paths are supported. It correctly distinguishes the roadmap's planned release from Learn's already-documented default experience, and keeps the undocumented administrator switch separate from the existing privacy preference.

claims.claim: The wave 2 prerequisite is documented for the Appearance tab, rather than as a prerequisite for the whole Personal settings redesign.

claims.quote: This tab isn't available if your system administrator selects the privacy preference for the entire organization in System Settings.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Every user running a model-driven app needs a licence providing Power Apps premium use rights.
claims.quote: Every user who runs a model-driven app needs a license that provides Power Apps premium use rights.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Power Apps Premium and Power Apps per app plans generally satisfy the premium use-rights requirement.
claims.quote: While Power Apps Premium, Power Apps per app plans, and the Power Apps per app pay-as-you-go meter that give premium Power Apps usage rights satisfy the requirement generally

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Use rights depend on the licence and the context in which the app runs.
claims.quote: use rights differ by license and by the context the app runs in.

claims.claim: The licensing model is included because Personal settings is an option within model-driven apps covered by the product's premium use-rights requirement.
claims.quote: Model-driven apps use Dataverse and are premium apps by default. Every user who runs a model-driven app needs a license that provides Power Apps premium use rights.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No licence, meter or charge specific to the Personal settings redesign is published.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Apps" "Personal settings" "licensing" "modern"; "modern" "personal settings" licensing price charge removal date. Read personal options and Power Apps licensing FAQs; no redesign-specific licence, meter or charge.

claims.claim: The roadmap and personal options page name no redesign-specific licence, meter or charge, and the personal options page lists no licence.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Apps" "Personal settings" "licensing" "modern". Read the supplied roadmap and complete Set personal options in model-driven apps page; neither names a redesign charge and the latter contains no licence requirement.

claims.where: controls[0].ui and controls[0].api; summary; Governance controls; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No administrator UI or API control is documented to enable or disable the modern Personal settings panel or hide its Switch to classic button.
claims.quote: Searched: "modern personal settings" "disable" "Switch to classic" admin; "Personal settings" "modern" "Organization" "API" Power Apps PowerShell PAC. Read personal options, privacy settings, behavior/PAC excerpts and searched Organization reference; no panel control.

claims.claim: The privacy preference is at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Privacy + Security > Privacy preferences > Default action to take when an error occurs.
claims.quote: select Manage. ... select Environments. ... select an environment. ... select Settings. ... Expand Product, and then select Privacy + Security. ... Under Privacy preferences, select a Default action to take when an error occurs.

claims.claim: The environment privacy setting lets administrators override users' error-reporting preferences for the entire organisation.
claims.quote: As an administrator, you can override their preferences and set error reporting preferences for the entire organization. You can prevent users from making changes in how errors are reported

claims.claim: Updating the privacy and security settings requires the System Administrator security role or equivalent permissions.
claims.quote: Make sure you have the System Administrator security role or equivalent permissions to update the settings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The sources describe no new data access for the Personal settings redesign.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Apps" "modern Personal settings" "data access" "autonomous". Read the roadmap description and full personal options page: the redesign describes organisation and navigation, not new data access.

claims.claim: The roadmap and personal options page describe no autonomous or agent capability for this redesign.
claims.quote: Searched: "Power Apps" "modern Personal settings" "data access" "autonomous". Read the supplied roadmap and full personal options page; neither describes an agent or autonomous capability for the redesign.

claims.claim: Learn does not give a specific removal date for classic Set Personal Options, saying only a future release.
claims.quote: Searched: "Personal settings" "classic" "removed" model-driven. Read personal options and deprecation search excerpts; personal options says "a future release" and no result gives a removal date for this dialog.
